text:
ryan: heads up — CI job `fused-attn:asan` started failing intermittently on ubuntu:gcc13 image. segfault in paged_attention::_compute_kv under ASAN. reproducible ~30% of runs. attaching short log.

jen: ugh, saw this locally once. which image tag exactly? gcc13 vs gcc12 differences have bitten us before.

ryan: image tag `redwood/build:bookworm-gcc13-cuda12`. log:
```
==1954321000==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000000 at pc 0x7f8a2c1a1b4e bp 0x7ffc9d2b22d0 sp 0x7ffc9d2b22c8
READ of size 8 at 0x0 thread T1
    #0 0x7f8a2c1a1b4d  (libflashkernel.so+0x11b4d) 
    #1 0x7f8a2c1a24f0 in paged_attention::_compute_kv(…) (libflashkernel.so+0x124f0)
    #2 0x561d3f4c2a7b in fused_forward

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV in libflashkernel.so
```

akshay: profile suggests KV cache miss spikes right before the crash. not sure if it's UAF or a bad kernel selection path. I can repro the miss pattern with perf and nvprof.

sonya: could be ABI mismatch — we recently bumped toolchain flags (ldflags shims) in the build image. libstdc++ in image != build host might give weird inline expectations. also check PACKED struct alignment in the kernel headers.

matt: adding to that, our autoselector sometimes picks `fused-kv` for seq_len=16 due to conservative heuristics; if the fused kernel was built with different alignment assumptions it could silently crash under ASAN. we should verify the compile flags used for kernels: -march, -mfma, -fno-stack-protector, and sanitizer flags.

jen: quick repro command I used:
```bash
docker run --rm -it redwood/build:bookworm-gcc13-cuda12 /bin/bash -c "export CC=gcc-13 CXX=g++-13; bazel build //runtime:flash_kernels --config=asan && ./bazel-bin/runtime/flash_kernels --bench paged --seq 16 --bs 8"
```

ci-bot: created issue redwood/runtime#4127 (link: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/issues/4127) and queued a debug job `fused-attn:asan-debug` (queued).

akshay: perf numbers that look related (from a small test run):
- before toolchain bump: p99 token latency ~42ms, KV cache hit rate 89%
- after bump + same image: p99 token latency ~68ms, KV cache hit rate 63%
Batch formation seems to change because of timing jitter; micro-batching pulled more small micro-batches which increases KV churn.

sonya: sounds like two issues tangled: (1) build/toolchain mismatch causing ASAN-visible crash in fused kernel; (2) runtime heuristic sensitivity causing perf regression after slight timing change. separate fixes.

jen: proposed plan:
1) For CI ASAN: pin gcc to 12 in an alternative ASAN job (non-blocking) so we have a stable baseline. add job that uses `bookworm-gcc12-cuda12` image.
2) Add an ASAN repro matrix that builds kernels with both gcc-12 and gcc-13 and runs the microbench for seq 8/16/64 with ASAN_OPTIONS=verbosity=1. capture full ASAN reports to artifacts.
3) Add unit test that forces autoselector into fused vs paged path so we can run kernel-specific CI for regressions.
4) Add small kernel build step that strips RPATH and uses static libstdc++ to avoid host/library mismatches.

matt: agree. also add a checklist to the packaging PR to ensure consistent -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE and identical -fpack-struct flags across all kernel builds.

ryan: I'll draft the CI changes and the repro matrix. assigning follow-ups: jen -> PR for pinned job + artifact capture, akshay -> perf microbench harness and KV miss trace, sonya -> investigate alignment/struct packing in kernel headers and try building kernels with -fno-common.

jen: opening PR now, will link here when ready. can we also add a flaky label to the current `fused-attn:asan` so it doesn't block releases until fixed? :thumbsup:

ryan: done — flagged as flaky and added the debug job. thanks everyone.

matt: FYI I ran the debug job once and reproduced the ASAN SEGV locally; stacktrace points to an assumption about 64-byte alignment for KV pages. adding alignment assert to help surface earlier.

sonya: good call. once we have deterministic repro we'll triage the kernel compile flags.

ci-bot: debug job completed (artifact uploaded: gs://redwood-ci/artifacts/1954321000/asan-debug.tar.gz).

akshay: leaving notes here: batching heuristics team - consider adding jitter-resistant shaping rules (min batch window) to avoid micro-batch thrash on small seq workloads.

ryan: wrapping up — created a short runbook in the issue with steps to reproduce and quick mitigations. we'll follow up in the PR.
